> Dear Students,
>
> Following the successful implementation of the first round of the
> Undergraduate Research Fellowship (URF), we invite proposals for
> Undergraduate Research Fellowship (URF) Round II.
>
> This fellowship is designed to further strengthen the research culture at
> TIET and support your academic and professional development. It encourages
> motivated undergraduate students to undertake innovative research projects
> under faculty mentorship, with the potential to lead to quality
> publications, patents or startups.
>
> *Fellowship Details:*
>
>    - Number of Fellowships: 100
>    - Fellowship Amount: Rs. 20,000 per annum
>    - Duration: 1 year
>
> *Eligibility Criteria:*
>
> Students who have already availed this fellowship are not eligible to
> apply again unless they have completed their current project and published
> a Scopus-indexed paper from it.
>
> *Team Option:*
>
> Students may apply either individually or as a team of two students under
> faculty mentorship.
>
> In case of a team application:
>
>    - The project will be treated as a single submission.
>    - The fellowship amount will be awarded collectively and will be
>    shared between the two students.
>    - A single student may apply with one or two faculty mentors.
>    - Two students can also apply with one faculty mentor.
>    - Two students can also apply with two different faculty mentors (same
>    department or different department).
>    - In any case a team of more than two students and two faculty mentors
>    is not allowed.
>
> *Application Process:*
>
> Interested students should:
>
>    1. Identify a research idea in their area of interest.
>    2. Discuss its feasibility with faculty member(s).
>    3. Determine the required resources and equipment.
>    4. Prepare a short research proposal under the guidance of the
>    mentor(s).
>    5. Submit the application through the following Google Form:
>
> https://forms.gle/hWfjC3gt7CZUzXx67
>
> Students without prior research experience are especially encouraged to
> apply and explore this opportunity.
>
> Please refer to the attached document for detailed information regarding
> the policy, application process, and proposal format.
>
> *Last date for submission:* May 30, 2026
>
> We encourage all interested students to apply and make the most of this
> opportunity to advance their research journey.
>
> *Evaluation Criteria*
>
> Applications will be assessed based on:
>
> ·         Quality, originality, and feasibility of the research proposal
>
> ·         Academic performance
>
> ·         Clarity of motivation and objectives
>
> ·         Strength of faculty mentor’s recommendation
>
> ·         Prior research experience or publications (if any)
>
> *Expectations from Fellows*
>
> ·         Engage actively and consistently with the faculty mentor.
>
> ·         Submit *quarterly progress reports *detailing research
> milestones.
>
> ·         Aim to publish research outcomes in reputed journals or
> conferences.
>
> ·         Demonstrate tangible outcomes such as publications, patents, or
> prototypes that strengthen your academic and professional profile.
>
>
>
> *For Students Without Prior Research Experience*
>
> Students new to research are strongly encouraged to participate. You can:
>
> ·         Identify an area of interest or problem you wish to explore.
>
> ·         Discuss ideas with potential faculty mentors for feasibility
> and scope.
>
> ·         Refine your concept into a focused research proposal.
>
> ·         Plan required resources and methodologies with guidance from
> your mentor.
>
> ·         This process will help you develop essential *research,
> analytical, and problem-solving skills *while transforming your ideas
> into impactful outcomes.
>
> ·         We encourage all motivated students to apply and take advantage
> of this opportunity to build your research experience and academic profile.
>
>
>
> NOTE:
>
> ü  *Each student is allowed to apply for only one project.*
>
> ü  *A faculty member may recommend a maximum of two project proposals

>

body:
*[DO NOT REVERT TO THIS EMAIL]*

Dear UG Students,

Hope that this email finds you well!

This is regarding the conduct of the *Mentor-Mentee program *at TIET.

The DoSA and DoAA offices have planned to execute the interaction session
between the faculty mentor and student mentee on *29th October 2025*. A
list of approx. 30 students has been tagged to each faculty member.
Students can view their personal information at the web kiosk under the
"Personal Info à Personal Details" link*.*

*Students must not discuss any generic grievances related to the hostel,
such as food, WiFi, or other similar issues. For this, one should contact
the hostel warden or the concerned authorities.*

*The following are the points related to the conduct of Mentor-Mentee Day:*

1.     The interaction schedule and other relevant details have been
provided to students through the web kiosk under the link "Personal Info" [A
screenshot has been attached to this email].

2.     This interaction is *mandatory *for all the *UG students.*

component of the student experience. From now onwards, the No Objection
Certificate (NOC) issued (from the DoAA Office) to students upon completion
of their program or issued for Training Internships, Visa, Bona-fide
Student, *etc*., will include a record as *Compliance / Non-compliance for

non-compliance will be noted in the NOC.

*.*

subject: Invitation for QUIZINGA!
body:
*“If it's witty, it's a quizinga.”*
~ *Sheldon Cooper (probably)*

Welcome to *Quizinga!*, a 2-day long quizzing fest organized by the *Thapar
Quizzing Club (tQc)!* This isn’t just your run-of-the-mill trivia showdown.
No, no. This is an intellectual decathlon, a grand arena where logic flexes
harder than your gym-going roommate, and deduction triumphs over dull
memorization. If you still need an additional incentive then a *prize pool
of **₹22K *awaits you.
Contrary to popular misconception, quizzing is *NOT about regurgitating
obscure facts* like a malfunctioning Wikipedia server. It’s about seeing
connections where others see chaos, following a trail of clues Sherlock
would be proud of. Here is the flow of events :

*Day 1: 19th April 2025 (Saturday):*

1. *SLUMDOG MELA-IONAIRE* - *Music Entertainment Literature Arts QUIZ*
🕒

*Time: 10:00 AM📍 Venue: MAIN AUDI❓ QMs: Aryan, Mridul & Nipun*

Prepare to sit in the hot seat as we bring you the 1st quiz of Quizinga —
SLUMDOG MELA-IONAIRE! This quiz is designed to test your *pop culture*
prowess, artistic flair, and literary wit. Whether you’re a *movie buff, a
bookworm, a music junkie, or an art aficionado*, Slumdog MELA-ionaire
promises a rollercoaster of fun, nostalgia, and discovery. Every question
brings you one step closer to becoming the ultimate MELA-ionaire! 🎶 🍿 📚
🎨

*2. AROUND THE WORLD IN 40 QUESTIONS* - *Travel Lifestyle Culture* QUIZ
🕑

*Time: 2:00 PM📍 Venue: MAIN AUDI❓ QMs: Praney & Yuvraj*
The next stop on your quizzing journey through the magical land of Quizinga
leads you to a trip like no other — AROUND THE WORLD IN 40 QUESTIONS!
Inspired by the spirit of exploration, this quiz challenges your knowledge
of world cuisines, iconic landmarks, diverse traditions, and the finer
things in life. Whether you're a jet-setter, a culture connoisseur, or a
couch traveler with a passion for learning about our wonderful world, this
quiz is your boarding pass to fun, fascination, and a few surprises along
the way. 🌎✈️

*Day 2: 20th April 2025 (Sunday):*

*A FISTFUL OF FUNDAES - **General Quiz*
🕑

*Time: 2:00 PM📍 Venue: LP - 101❓ QMs: Abhinav & Ankur*
We wrap up the final day of our event with a ‘Big Bang’ — the third and
final quiz: A FISTFUL OF FUNDAES. Curated and hosted by none other than
Abhinav and Ankur, two legends of the Thapar Quizzing Club, this quiz marks
the *homecoming of our veterans.* From art to sports, space to politics,
food to tech — and everything under the sun — it’s all fair game in this
general quiz, where logic and instinct meet. Get ready to put your fundaes
to the test and enjoy the spirit of quizzing with a fistful of fun! 🏆
Join us at Quizinga, where every question is a new adventure, and it’s not
about having all the answers, but enjoying the quest for them.
Happy Quizzing ✨
Thapar Quizzing Club (tQc)

                      Get personalized guidance from mentors and collaborate in active discussion groups with peers throughout your journey.

                       Contests & Workshops

                      Compete in intra-community contests and workshops and boost your skills, gain recognition, and win prizes.

Dear Students

The Erasmus Mundus MESPOM Scholarship Program 2026–2028 is now accepting
applications. Four top universities—Central European University (Austria),
Lund University (Sweden), the University of Manchester (UK), and the
University of the Aegean (Greece)—offer the esteemed Erasmus Mundus Joint
Master’s Degree known as MESPOM (Master’s in Environmental Science, Policy,
and Management). For the duration of the study, this fully financed program
pays for living expenses, meals, tuition, travel, and a visa. The MESPOM
program prepares students for worldwide careers in environmental management
and policy by offering a distinctive international learning experience.
Here are specific details about the application procedure, semester order,
and program structure.

Eligibility Criteria :

   - All nationalities are welcome to apply.
   - A bachelor’s degree in a related discipline, such as engineering,
   management, policy, environmental sciences, or the natural or social
   sciences, is required.
   - If they have professional or volunteer experience that demonstrates a
   strong dedication to environmental issues, candidates from different
   academic backgrounds are also eligible.
   - Proficiency in English is necessary.

Austria, Sweden, the United Kingdom, and Greece are the host nations.

Erasmus Mundus Joint Master of Environmental Sciences, Policy, and
Management (MESPOM) is the name of the program.

Master’s degree levels at universities: Four European universities jointly
offer

Organization of Funding: European Union

Benefits :

   - Travel Costs
   - Visa Charges
   - Living Allowance per Month
   - Grant for Installation
   - Allowance for Subsistence
   - Complete Coverage of Tuition

Deadline: 7th January 2026

body:

Namaste,

*Greetings from Chhatra Sansad India.*

We feel proud to share InternNation Leadership Tour with you, an
initiative taken
by a youth run non-profit organisation. This leadership tour will be
interned by 45 delegates coming in from the Top Educational Institutes of
our country.

About InternNation Leadership Tour.

InternNation is an immersive hands-on learning program for the youth of
today who wish to one day be stalwarts in their own right and have the will
to change the very foundation of our Society.

Through InternNation, Chhatra Sansad provides the delegates with a chance
to meet and interact with Visionaries from the Public and Private Sector as
well as the Government so that they can learn from the very best and
inspire their fellow Indians. We provide first-hand experience to the
various governance models, opportunity to interact with leaders behind the
scene and learn how they do what they do.

InternNation is a 7 day tour of* Delhi, Dehradun & Mussorrie*. The
participants will get a chance to imbibe the same values that drive today’s
leaders and Visionaries. Additionally, they will be spending 7 days with
likeminded people with the same energy and enthusiasm as them and who share
a similar vision as them. This Tour also serves as a pathway to network
with Policy Makers and Government officials for future collaboration and be
a source of constant communication.

*In 2025, our delegates had the privilege of interacting with esteemed
ministers and leaders, including  Aaditya Thackeray, Ashish Shelar,
Chandrakant Patil, Atul Save, Desmond D'Costa, Vijai Sardesai, Shripad
Yesso Naik, and Nilesh Cabral as well as inspiring industry leaders such as
Sundararaman Ramamurthy, Devita Saraf, Niranjan Hiranandani, Vishal, Pramod
Kumar, and Suneeta Shetty. Additionally, they had enriching interactions
with renowned personalities like Piyush Mishra, Jackie Shroff, and Ajinkya
Naik, gaining invaluable insights into leadership, governance, and
innovation from diverse fields.They also engaged with key officials such as
Smt. Sangeeta S. Naik, Ms. Prajakta Goltekar, Advocate General Devidas
Pangam.*

*In 2024, the delegates had the incredible opportunity to meet and interact
with several influential figures, including Shri Aditya Thackeray, Smt.
Smriti Irani, Dr. Kiran Bedi, Sundaraman Ramamurthy, Shri Ramesh Bais, Shri
Rahul Narwekar, Dr. Anil Jain, Arnab Goswami, Anand Narasimhan, actors
Naseeruddin Shah and Ratna Pathak Shah, Shashi Ruia, Ms. Meghna Ghai Puri,
and Vice Admiral A. N. Pramod. This diverse array of leaders, from
politics, business, media, and the arts, offered delegates invaluable
insights and inspiration.*

*In 2023, delegates had the unique opportunity to engage with a diverse
array of influential personalities, fostering meaningful interactions.
Notable figures such as Nitin Gadkari, Ranjan Gogoi, Atishi Marlena, Swati
Maliwal, Anand Narasimhan, Rajdeep Sardesai, Bhupinder Hooda, Deepinder
Hooda, Charanjit Singh Channi, B K Shivani, Temjeng Along, and Charu Pragya
were part of the enriching discourse. Their presence brought a wealth of
perspectives, contributing to a dynamic and insightful exchange during the
event.*

45 delegates from across the nation met with influential figures in August
2022, including Dr. CN Ashwath Narayan, Piyush Mishra, Neerja Birla, Ashish
Chauhan, Bhagat Singh Koshyari, Kirit Somaiya, Varun Grover, Jacky
Bhagnani, Charu Pragya, Savio Rogriguez, Thawar Chand Gehlot, Kiran Bedi,
Aishwarya Mahadev.

Subramanian Swamy, Piyush Goyal, Smriti Irani, Narendra Tomar, Parshottam

Uday Mahurkar, and Swati Maliwal were among the role models we met on our
January trip to Delhi, Lucknow, Ayodhya, and Varanasi.

This Leadership Tour will involve various activities, exercises and
projects that will be carried out by the participants, giving them much
needed experience in Governance, Communication and Organisation. These
activities will vary on a day to day basis to help create an all round
individual adept at the intricacies and workings of Leadership and
Governance. Each delegate will make a report for the same, which will be
sent to the PM Office and Niti Ayog.

*THAPAR INSTITUTE OF ENGINEERING AND TECHNOLOGY, PATIALA*

*CIRCULAR FOR CONDUCT AND ETHICS FOR STUDENTS*

*INTRODUCTION*

This is a circular for conduct to be adhered by all students enrolled with
Thapar Institute of Engineering and Technology, Patiala (hereinafter
referred to as Institute) for pursuing various courses. It is incumbent on
all students to abide by the circular. It shall be applicable to all
students enrolled with the Institute as a matter of daily routine as well
as during Institute  sponsored activities, functions hosted by other
recognized organizations as well as any off-campus activity that has
implications on the reputations of the Institute. The entire premises of
the Institute including but not limited to parks, lawns, corridors,
washroom, canteen etc. any place within the campus shall fall within the
ambit of this circular.

*ETHICS AND CONDUCT*

This makes it incumbent on all students to adhere to the following: -

1.     All students shall be properly attired and groomed in keeping with
the dignity and decorum of the Institute as well as culture and values of
the community. Decent and formal dress code that makes the environment of
learning conducive for students from different backgrounds and cultures is
imperative. As a general rule, your dressing sense should reflect our
Indian culture and ethos.

2.     The Institute believes in safeguarding the morality and culture of
the community. In order to maintain a professional atmosphere of learning
and mutual respect, all students will refrain from inappropriate and
intimate behavior in Institute premises. No student shall indulge in an
indecent act involving Public Display of Affection in a way that the same
becomes a cause of nuisance for any third person. Any violation of this
circular shall entail disciplinary action.

3.     The Institute believes in promoting a safe environment by enforcing
behavioral standards. All students must uphold academic integrity, respect
all persons and their rights and property and safety of others.

4.     All students must deter from indulging in any and all forms of
misconduct including partaking in any activity off-campus which can affect
the Institute's interests and reputation substantially.

5.     Kindly note that the Institute will take measures to impose the said
conduct and ethics code.

(Padmakumar Nair)

Director

body:
To Sir/mam ,

Greetings from Piramal Foundation!

I am Avneet Kaur, Program Leader from Piramal Foundation, part of the
Gandhi Fellowship Program Team. I am writing to introduce the Gandhi
Fellowship to your esteemed college. It gives me immense pleasure to
announce the initiation of recruitment drive for Gandhi Fellowship Batch
18, starting in 2025.

I am writing to share a proposal for engaging with all the *Thapar
Institute of Engineering & Technology Students *to introduce the Gandhi
Fellowship Program for Batch 18 recruitment. This program is a
transformative opportunity for final-year UG and PG students, equipping
them with leadership skills, grassroots exposure, and the vision to
contribute to nation-building through impactful roles in social and public
systems.

To maximize participation and accommodate the diverse schedules of campuses:

we can organize *online interactive sessions* to ensure all students have
access to this opportunity.

We believe these sessions will provide valuable insights into the Gandhi
Fellowship Program, its objectives, and the career development
opportunities it offers.

I kindly request your support in sharing this proposal. Additionally, we
would appreciate your assistance in coordinating dates and formats for
these sessions.

Additionally, I kindly request your support in sharing the Gandhi
Fellowship application link with your students to help them explore this
transformative program:

*Apply at Gandhi Fellowship (2025-27):*
https://aspire.gandhifellowship.org/application-process/apply/1978

*Gandhi Fellowship Website:*
https://gandhifellowship.org/

I am also attaching the following documents for your kind reference:

   - Brochure about the Gandhi Fellowship Program
   - E-Posters of the Gandhi Fellowship Program that can be circulated in
   your WhatsApp/email groups.

*Eligibility Criteria for Gandhi Fellowship:*

   - Should be within the age group of 21 to 25
   - A graduate/final-year student with a minimum average of 55% in 10th,
   12th, and UG/PG

*A brief Note on the Gandhi Fellowship Program*

In 2008, the Piramal Foundation started a 23-month program to foster a
Fellowship of the youth of India. The premise was that these young people
would build cultures, not just products. They would be a blend of vision
and values and be role models beyond work. They would do more than
harvesting outcomes – they would cultivate communities. Today the Gandhi
Fellowship is well acknowledged program that selects the best from among
the inspired and inventive young people from India’s top college and
universities to help them develop into great leaders. The path to the
purpose is through a 4-semester practical, grassroots immersion curriculum.

 *Work of Gandhi Fellows*

What started as a particle is today a wave. Over 1000+ Gandhi Fellows work
across India at block and district levels in the bottommost 300+ districts
and in some cases in state capitals. Their work entails engaging with
government stakeholders and communities for implementing societal programs
– in spaces such as water, health and education.

Functioning on the intersections of *Samaj, Bazar and Sarkar – society,
business and the government *– the Fellows aim to develop understanding and
empathy for the last-mile citizens as they learn to negotiate improved
services for them. In the process, they not only encounter struggles of the
commonplace Indian but also confront their own inner obstacles – and learn
to minimize if not entirely transcend both.

Coming from different persuasions and preferences, the Fellows begin to
introspect their challenges and motives. In what is intended to be a
process of self-discovery, the Fellowship team facilitates the young people
to delve deep within for personal change and devise ways of converting
private dreams into public reality.

The Fellows receive on-site coaching and mentoring to help negotiate
problems as well as discern solutions. The Fellowship holds
transformational experiences for youth to:

   - Augment their career choices in alignment with 21st century
   opportunities
   - Help them innovate and deploy their own bottom-of-the-pyramid solutions
   - Sensitize them to the problems facing India and the larger humanity
   - Help develop an informed, sensitive and effective global citizenship.

 *Youth towards Nation Building and Self Development*

It is beyond doubt that the Indian human resource is at par with the best
in the world. But students from top western education institutions are
harnessing their energies towards breaking new ground – be it solar,
climate change, health, education, democracy, social equity. Our brightest
minds are queuing up in the placement market rather than exploring the
excitement of becoming adventurers, thinkers, inventors and leaders. What
is missing here is, contemporary methods of learning beyond the classroom.
What is also missing is the dare to go beyond the familiar. We believe
young people, who have been exposed to quality education need to take up
leadership roles in society. They owe it to themselves, most of all.

 I urge you to introduce the Fellowship by forwarding this letter to
teachers across the campus and introduce us to students who want to accept
this dare – and contribute to social and public systems change, besides
politics, academia, media and the corporate world. In the coming decades,
we see ourselves developing a pipeline of leaders, builders of solutions
for Building Bharat. We are optimistic that this network will be future
collaborators in articulating problems of not just a burgeoning India but
also re-visioning and developing judicious solutions for an entire planet.

 *A Small Grant*

We support our Fellows with a small grant of INR 24,500/- per month while
underwriting board, lodging and communications costs.

I can assure you your students and our future Fellows are here to find not
just the best jobs but also worthy roles in society.

 We look forward to your support and collaboration.

Thank you for your time and support. I look forward to your collaboration.

Warm regards,

*Warm Regards*

*Avneet Kaur*

*Program Leader-Marketing & Recruitment*
